title: Personal Checking: Refund Amount for an Overdraft Item Fee Charged in Error
content:
## How the grounds combine and what is paid back

The latest overdraft item fee on a Personal Checking account is a bank error as soon as any one ground of error holds; the grounds are alternatives, not requirements to be met together.

- **Bank error, not yet refunded:** the whole fee comes back, at the exact figure on the fee entry, and the refund is recorded with bank error as its reason. There is no partial refund.
- **Already refunded:** once a refund entry exists against the fee, no further refund is made on any ground.
- **No ground holds:** this policy returns nothing. A goodwill request is then weighed against the courtesy tests that ordinary Personal Checking fee refunds must pass.

Fees are booked to the cent, so the refund is never rounded.

## Outcome grid

| At least one ground holds | Prior refund entry | Amount refunded here |
|---|---|---|
| yes | none | fee amount in full |
| yes | present | 0.00 |
| no | none | 0.00 |
| no | present | 0.00 |

## Hypothetical example

A 29.00 USD overdraft item fee with no earlier refund, charged on a debit that a transfer would have paid, is refunded at 29.00 USD. The same fee, already refunded as a courtesy last week, receives nothing more.
